identity.real_world_identity_notes: The FIA record establishes the homologated Audi V8 quattro identity. A reputable period retrospective describes a fully synchronized six-speed gearbox; exact AMS2 gate and technique were established by guided testing.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed round rim without integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: With assists disabled, selecting first without clutch produced only a slight roll followed immediately by a stall; the standing-start clutch is therefore required.
All six H-pattern positions directly selected their gears.
Clutchless upshifts worked after lifting the throttle, and clutchless downshifts worked without an automatic blip.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
Guided test completed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled and no separate throttle-blip assist available.
The slight first-gear roll did not constitute successful move-off because the engine immediately stalled.

confidence.basis: Exact identity, move-off, six direct H-pattern gears, shift technique, and cockpit wheel were directly verified; independent historical sources support identity and synchronized six-speed construction.

claims.basis: Official identity context and exact live telemetry agree.
Historical documentation specifies a synchronized six-speed gearbox and the guided test directly selected all six H-pattern gears.
Guided current-game testing directly established these behaviors and cockpit details.

driver_summary: A fully synchronised six-speed, stated by period documentation rather than assumed, so the blip eases the synchros but the gear engages without it.
